message: legacy float label has no IR value representation
why: This is a legacy-tag defense line, not a ban on floating point. Since v2.0.0 the only floating type is `double` (IEEE-754 binary64) and literals are emitted as the bit pattern {"k":"double","bits":"<16 lowercase hex digits>"}; IR bytes contain no JSON floating-point numbers, so V-7 / canonical / signing all hold. A LitExpr tagged "float" is the pre-v2.0.0 shape: it falls into the string fallback and produces {"t":"string","v":"float"} — valid IR that silently returns the string "float" at runtime. The three scanners stay as defense in depth against C ABI callers that ignore diagnostics.
fix: use `double` for floating-point values (literals 1.5 / 1.5e2 / 1e3 are supported)
keep money in `cost` / int micro-units; the `json.as_float` API name is unchanged
